what_its_for: Glyburide is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults with type 2 diabetes. It works by helping your pancreas make more insulin, which lowers the amount of sugar in your blood. It is used along with a healthy diet and exercise to manage your diabetes.
how_to_take: Take glyburide by mouth, usually once a day with breakfast or the first main meal of your day. If your doctor has you taking it twice a day, take the second dose with your evening meal. Swallow the tablet whole or you may break it in half if needed. Always take it with food to help prevent low blood sugar. Take it at the same time every day to help you remember.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it based on how well your blood sugar is controlled. The usual starting dose is 2.5 to 5 mg once daily. The maximum dose is typically 20 mg per day. Never change your dose on your own without talking to your doctor or pharmacist first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still close to the time of your regular dose. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one, as this can cause your blood sugar to drop too low.
storage: Store glyburide at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medication after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking glyburide, as it can cause your blood sugar to drop dangerously low or cause an unpleasant flushing reaction. Avoid skipping meals or eating less than usual, as this increases your risk of low blood sugar. Be careful with high-sugar foods and drinks that can spike your blood sugar. Use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors, as glyburide can make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Tell your doctor before starting any new medications, including over-the-counter drugs and supplements, as many can affect your blood sugar.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience signs of low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) such as shaking, sweating, dizziness, rapid heartbeat, confusion, blurred vision, or fainting. Also call your doctor if you have signs of high blood sugar such as increased thirst, frequent urination, or blurry vision. Seek immediate help for signs of a serious allergic reaction including rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing. Contact your doctor if you develop yellowing of the skin or eyes, unusual bruising or bleeding, or severe stomach pain.
when_it_works: Glyburide starts working within a few hours of taking your first dose, and you may notice your blood sugar levels begin to improve within the first few days. However, it may take several weeks to see the full benefit. Continue taking it every day as prescribed, even if you feel well. Your doctor will check your blood sugar and HbA1c levels regularly to make sure the medication is working properly.
special_populations: Older adults (age 65 and above): Use with extra caution. Older adults are at higher risk for low blood sugar, which can be more dangerous and harder to recognize. A lower starting dose is often recommended. Kidney or liver problems: Glyburide may not be safe if you have moderate to severe kidney or liver disease, as it can build up in your body and cause serious low blood sugar. Tell your doctor about any kidney or liver issues. Pregnancy: Glyburide is generally not recommended during pregnancy. Talk to your doctor about safer options for managing blood sugar if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if glyburide passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while on this medication. Children: Glyburide is not approved for use in children.
